# Lane D1: identity-feature ablation

**Offline only.** Nothing here touches `ml/out/models` (the shipped
artifacts), the live app, Vertex Model Registry, or Gemini. Every run
reuses `ml.evaluate.run_scope` and `ml.evaluate.XGB_PARAMS` unmodified
-- same hyperparameters, same seed base, same grouped 5-fold CV, as
shipped Model A. Only the feature set passed to `run_scope` changes.

**Data and rates below are synthetic**, generated by our own
`simulator/`, not observed real-world behaviour. Base rates in
particular reflect a design choice this project's own generator makes
about how often it assigns a ring member a reused device/document --
not a measurement of how real money-mule rings actually behave.

## Gate: does `all16` reproduce shipped Model A?

| | PR-AUC | false alerts / catch @80% recall |
|---|---|---|
| shipped (`model_a_metadata.json`) | 0.6220 | 1.968 |
| this run (`all16`, 3-seed mean) | 0.6220 | 1.968 |

**Passed.** (Seed-42-only numbers in the run log show 0.6176/2.102 --
within the same seed-to-seed spread already documented elsewhere in
this repo; the 3-seed mean matches shipped exactly to 4 decimal
places.)

## Headline: how much of Model A depends on identity data

| T=5m | PR-AUC | recall @1% FPR | false alerts / catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `all16` (shipped Model A) | 0.622 ± 0.004 | 0.617 ± 0.009 | 1.97 ± 0.10 |
| `drop_all_identity` (= Model B, transfer-only) | **0.245 ± 0.004** | 0.268 ± 0.006 | 11.88 ± 0.42 |
| `identity_only` (4 features) | 0.471 ± 0.002 | 0.479 ± 0.008 | 15.93 ± 1.02 |
| `drop_all_identity_and_age` (transfer-only minus account age) | **0.071 ± 0.0004** | 0.033 ± 0.0007 | 15.83 ± 0.21 |

| T=180m | PR-AUC | recall @1% FPR | false alerts / catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `all16` | 0.988 ± 0.001 | 0.985 ± 0.002 | 0.00 |
| `drop_all_identity` | 0.975 ± 0.001 | 0.974 ± 0.003 | 0.0035 |
| `identity_only` | 0.514 ± 0.002 | 0.534 ± 0.006 | 12.84 ± 0.93 |
| `drop_all_identity_and_age` | 0.971 ± 0.001 | 0.965 ± 0.004 | 0.0029 |

**The plain statement: at T=5m, removing identity data collapses PR-AUC
from 0.622 to 0.245 -- 39% of the shipped number. At T=180m it barely
matters (0.988 -> 0.975).** Model A's early-detection advantage -- the
thing that lets a ring be caught before money reaches the exit, which
is the operational point of the 5-minute horizon -- depends heavily on
identity reuse. By three hours, accumulated transfer behaviour alone
is almost enough on its own.

**`identity_only` (just 4 features) beats `drop_all_identity` (12
features) on PR-AUC at T=5m (0.471 vs. 0.245).** Four identity
features carry more early-detection signal than the entire
transfer-graph feature set. Identity reuse is not a minor supplement
to Model A -- at this horizon it is the dominant signal.

**`drop_all_identity_and_age` is the most unflattering number in this
experiment: PR-AUC 0.071 at T=5m, barely above a coin flip on this
base rate.** Model B's already-modest 0.245 is itself propped up
substantially by `account_age_days` -- an account *attribute*, not a
transfer *behaviour*. Pull that one feature out of the transfer-only
set and almost nothing is left at T=5m. "Transfer-only" detection at
the early horizon is not really detecting transfer *patterns* so much
as leaning on how old the account is.

## Per-feature and paired-drop breakdown (redundancy check), T=5m

| drop | PR-AUC | Δ from all16 |
|---|---|---|
| `drop_device_count` (device_count alone) | 0.616 | −0.006 |
| `drop_shared_device_count` (alone) | 0.527 | −0.095 |
| `drop_document_reuse_count` (alone) | 0.465 | −0.157 |
| `drop_document_reuse_flag` (alone) | 0.620 | −0.002 |
| `drop_device_pair` (both device features) | **0.489** | −0.133 |
| `drop_document_pair` (both document features) | **0.389** | −0.233 |

Both pairs show real redundancy: dropping `device_count` alone costs
almost nothing (−0.006) and dropping `shared_device_count` alone costs
more (−0.095), but dropping **both together** (−0.133) costs more than
either single drop -- each one partly covers for the other's absence,
so a single-feature ablation understates how much the pair jointly
matters. Same pattern, more pronounced, for the two document features:
`document_reuse_flag` is nearly redundant with `document_reuse_count`
alone (−0.002, since the flag is literally derived from the count),
but removing both together still costs more than removing the count
alone (−0.233 vs. −0.157) -- some information is carried by having
both forms available to the tree, not just one.

## Base rates in the generator (full 30,000 accounts, full window)

| group | n | device_count>1 | shared_device_count>0 | any document reuse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ring members (any role) | 899 | 46.1% | 38.4% | 37.3% |
| non-ring | 29,101 | 20.5% | 9.7% | 6.3% |
| bank span 1 | 240 | 45.0% | 37.1% | 35.8% |
| bank span 2 | 381 | 45.4% | 37.3% | 38.1% |
| bank span 3 | 278 | 47.8% | 41.0% | 37.4% |

Ring members are **4-6x** more likely to show device or document reuse
than non-ring accounts (shared device: 38.4% vs. 9.7%; document reuse:
37.3% vs. 6.3%). The rate is essentially flat across bank span (1, 2,
or 3 banks) -- the generator assigns reuse as a property of ring
membership itself, not something that emerges from or scales with how
many banks a ring touches. **This is a generator design choice, not an
empirical finding about real money-mule behaviour** -- our simulator
decided ring members reuse devices/documents at roughly this rate; a
real ring's actual reuse rate is unknown and could be higher or lower.

## What this means for real banks

If real banks cannot share device or KYC identity fields across
institutions -- which is the realistic constraint this project's own
`docs/data_sharing.md` and the Confidential Space enclave exist to
work around -- then a cross-bank detector limited to transfer-only
features faces the `drop_all_identity` numbers above, not the shipped
`all16` numbers: PR-AUC 0.245 instead of 0.622 at the 5-minute horizon,
with nearly 6x the false alerts per catch (11.9 vs. 2.0). The 3-hour
horizon is far more forgiving (0.975 vs. 0.988), so a bank that can
tolerate slower detection loses much less by going transfer-only than
one that needs the early catch. This is the honest trade this
submission's shipped Model A already makes implicitly by including
identity features at all; this ablation puts a number on exactly how
much that choice is worth, and at which horizon it matters most.
